newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks climb to new record on GDP joy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks climb to new record on GDP joy.

text.p: Mexican stocks notched their fourth record close in six sessions after strong economic data sent local and foreign bulls into the market, traders said.

"There's a virtuous circle in the economy which offers a bright outlook for this year, which the bourse (market) translated into a rally," said Rodolfo Campuzano, an analyst at the Invex brokerage in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index closed up 32.34 points, or 0.84 percent, at 3,875.04.
Volume was heavy at 115 million shares traded and reflected greater participation by foreign brokers, traders said.

Mexico's Finance Ministry announced shortly before the opening bell rang that full-year 1996 gross domestic product was up 5.1 percent from 1995, and fourth-quarter figures were up 7.6 percent in year-ago terms.
A prior Reuters survey of Mexico City financial firms showed average predicted increases of 4.65 percent for the year and 5.25 percent for the final quarter.
Dealers drew attention to an ebullient mood on the trading floor, where they shouted and elbowed their way to settle an unusually high number of 6,109 trades.
"Dealing was heavy, it was a fun session. Foreigners had a field day," one trader said.
Telecommunications firm Telmex and retail stock Cifra led the rally, traders said. Telmex L shares and Cifra B and C shares accounted for one-quarter of all shares traded.
Telmex L shares ended up 24 centavos (three cents) at 15.72 pesos ($2.02), and Cifra B shares gained 28 centavos (4 cents) to 12.20 pesos ($1.57).
In New York, Telmex American Depository Receipts fended off a slide in the Dow Jones industrial average to end up 3/4 at 40-3/4, a level unseen since the December 1994 peso crisis.
Dealers said Cifra gained on news it was to propose a dividend to its shareholders and on stock upgrades from international brokerages.
On the broad market, 128 stocks changed hands. Gainers outnumbered decliners 71 to 26.
Cellular phone company Iusacell was the biggest loser, off 84 centavos (11 cents) at 8.50 pesos ($1.09).
Traders said dealers sold Iusacel stock after the company reported a net loss for 1996 during the session.
Technical analysts noted that the IPC receded from an intraday record of 3,912.66 points set in early trade.

"The IPC is overbought, and several indicators are looking tired. After today's rally, a rest would be good for the market to gather steam before gaining once more," said Jaime Fernandez, an analyst with the Interacciones brokerage.
"Nonetheless, I think it should return to 3,750 points to take a run at the 4,000-point mark. It's not the bullet that kills you, but how fast it's shot," he added.
